title: Usas: A Sustainable Continuous-Learning Framework for Edge Servers
problem: Edge servers use compressed models prone to data drift, and continuous training at deployment scale has unsustainable aggregate power demands on grid supply.
motivation: Edge servers must perform continuous learning to maintain accuracy while operating sustainably under renewable energy constraints.
method: Usas enables sustainable training through three strategies: optimizing the training algorithms, co-designing the hardware and software together, and using morphable acceleration hardware (processors that dynamically reconfigure based on available power). The morphable accelerator changes its computing capacity based on real-time solar power—running at full strength in sunlight and scaling down when clouds block the sun—letting continuous training run entirely on renewable energy instead of drawing from the power grid.
key_novelty: Morphable acceleration hardware (specialized processors that automatically change their capabilities based on solar power availability) enables edge servers to continuously update their AI models entirely on renewable energy.
contributions: Algorithmic and hardware-software co-design approach for continuous learning on resource-constrained edge servers
Morphable accelerator that dynamically adapts to solar variance and power availability
4.96% mean accuracy improvement over prior continuous learning approaches
Energy savings of 234.95 kWH/year per edge-server versus DNN accelerators

metrics.energy_or_tops_w: 234.95 kWH/year vs DNN accelerator; 2.63 MWH/year vs data center GPU

limitations: Evaluation limited to real-world traffic dataset; generalization to diverse workloads and edge deployment scenarios not discussed.
primary_theme: Sustainable edge computing with renewable power adaptation
